transcript.text: Bosch HBS534BS0B oven displaying E011 and won't let me do anything. Beeping. Help!

E011 cannot be confirmed reliably as one specific fault for this Bosch oven: published meanings conflict. With the constant beeping and no response, the leading possibility is a button being detected as held down, or a fault in the control-panel/touch-key assembly. A temporary control-electronics glitch is also possible. 1. Switch the oven off at the cooker isolator switch or fuse box and leave it off for five minutes. Then restore power. This clears a control lock-up; if E011 returns straight away, it is less likely to be a one-off glitch. 2. With the oven isolated, wipe the control area with a barely damp cloth and dry it thoroughly. Do not spray cleaner directly onto it. Press each button once, individually, checking whether one feels physically stuck, unusually stiff, or does not click/respond like the others. Moisture, grease or a stuck key can cause continuous beeping. 3. Once powered back on, look for a key/lock symbol. If one is shown, use the manual’s lock-release instruction; a lock can prevent normal operation, though it would not usually explain persistent beeping. If the code returns immediately after the reset and the controls remain unresponsive, stop trying to operate it. It will normally need an appliance engineer to diagnose the control panel first, with the control module only considered after that. Do not remove the oven casing or attempt internal electrical checks.

Did the reset: off at the cooker switch for 5 mins, dried the panel with a towel first, and it came back up normally with no code. Heated to 180C fine too. Was there still a bit of spray residue along the bottom edge, so I guess that was it?

Yes — that is a very plausible cause. Spray residue along the lower edge can creep into or bridge the control-panel area, making the oven think a button is being held down. That fits the E011, beeping and unresponsive controls, and the fact it reset and then heated normally after drying. For future cleaning, switch the oven off and let the panel cool, spray cleaner onto a cloth rather than directly at the fascia, then wipe and dry around the edges. If E011 returns when the panel is dry and has not been cleaned, the control panel itself may be starting to fail and would be worth having assessed. For now, as it is operating normally, no repair is indicated.

candidates: Stuck or failed control-panel button/touch panel (high)

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Bosch; model HBS534BS0B; code E011.
The fault they reported is: "beeping and unresponsive controls". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

candidates: Moisture or cleaning-spray residue affecting the control panel / causing a false held-button detection (high)
plan: They asked: "Was the spray residue along the bottom edge likely the cause?" - answer that first.
The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.
